reasoning_traces.think:
Theorem D establishes equivalence of two set functions v and λ induced by mean fundamental sequences of integrable simple functions converging in measure to the same limit. The proof hinges on uniform absolute continuity (Theorem C), ensuring that differences in integrals vanish as sequence indices grow. This allows extension from finite-measure sets to σ-finite ones via countable additivity. The core insight is that convergence in measure implies convergence of associated indefinite integrals, provided the underlying functions are simple and integrable. The breakdown occurs when either the convergence condition fails or the σ-finiteness assumption is violated, leading to non-identical set functions.
